request.prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural. One real photograph for a Spanish-speaking adult beginner learning English. Natural everyday photographic detail, real material, fabric, metal and fur texture, soft natural daylight and correct perspective; NOT an illustration, 3D render, cartoon, collage, cutout or app UI. Full-bleed 3:2 landscape; no frames, padding, blur bands, vignette, watermark or captions. No letters, words, numbers, logos or brand marks anywhere, including on clothing, collars, bags, vehicles, plates and walls. A first-time learner must understand the picture instantly on a small phone screen.

This is a precise edit of image 1: the result must look like a second photograph taken from the same spot a moment later, with the same framing, perspective, lens and light, and with every kept object in the same place at the same size. Change only what the instruction names.

Image 1 shows a brand-new blue car. Keep the same car model, the same blue color, the same camera angle, the same position and size in the frame, and the same driveway and garage wall. Show the SAME car many years later as a clearly USED car. Its paint is dull, faded and chalky with no shine and no reflections; there are several long pale scratches and two shallow dents on the front door and the front wing; the front bumper is scuffed and scraped at its corner; there are small rust spots along the wheel arch and the bottom of the doors; the headlights are cloudy and yellowed; the windows are dusty; the wheels are dull grey with dark brake dust and one scraped rim; the tires are worn and dusty; dried mud is splashed low on the body. The wear is obvious at a glance even when the photo is very small. It is an ordinary used car that still drives: nothing is broken off, crashed, burnt or missing, the glass is whole and all four tires are full. The front plate stays a blank plain white rectangle. Exactly one car; no people, no other vehicles, no price tag and no signs.

cost.basis: Reported usage at list prices checked 2026-09-24; before tax, not an invoice.
